sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Latitudes and Longitudes** are imaginary geographical grid lines drawn on the globe to locate places precisely.
Concept formalized during the ancient Greek period by **Eratosthenes** and **Hipparchus**; standardized globally in **1884** (Prime Meridian).
**Geographers and Cartographers** developed the coordinate system; **Sir Sandford Fleming** proposed standard time zones.
Crucial for **navigation, time calculation, mapping, weather forecasting, and identifying climatic zones** on Earth.
Latitudes are parallel horizontal circles; Longitudes are vertical semi-circles converging at the poles.
Latitudes include **Equator, Tropics, and Polar Circles**; Longitudes include **Prime Meridian and International Date Line**.
High-scoring static GK area in **UP Assistant Teacher (Environmental & Social Studies)** exam covering time zones and coordinates.
Total latitudes equal **181**; total longitudes equal **360**; 1 degree longitude equals **4 minutes** of time difference.

items.title: 1. Latitudes (Parallels of Latitude)
items.content:
• **Definition:** Angular distance of a point north or south of the **Equator**, measured in degrees.
• **Shape:** Complete circles running from **east to west**.
• **Length:** Decreases progressively from the **Equator (0°)** to zero at the **Poles (90°N/90°S)**.
• **Total Count:** **181** (Equator + 90 Northern parallels + 90 Southern parallels).
• **Spacing:** Distance between two consecutive latitudes is approximately **111 km** everywhere.

items.title: 2. Important Latitudinal Lines
items.content:
• **Equator (0°):** Divides the Earth into **Northern and Southern Hemispheres**.
• **Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N):** Marks the northernmost limit of the **Sun's direct overhead rays**.
• **Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S):** Marks the southernmost limit of the **Sun's direct overhead rays**.
• **Arctic Circle (66.5° N):** Boundary of the **Northern Frigid Zone**.
• **Antarctic Circle (66.5° S):** Boundary of the **Southern Frigid Zone**.
• **Mnemonic:** **E**very **T**ime **C**ats **A**nswer, **T**hey **A**lways **C**heck (**E**quator, **T**ropic of **C**ancer, **A**rctic, **T**ropic of **C**apricorn, **A**ntarctic, **C**ircle).

items.title: 3. Longitudes (Meridians of Longitude)
items.content:
• **Definition:** Angular distance measured east or west of the **Prime Meridian (0°)**.
• **Shape:** Semi-circles running from the **North Pole to the South Pole**.
• **Length:** All meridians are **equal in length** (approx. 20,000 km each).
• **Total Count:** **360** (180 in Eastern Hemisphere, 180 in Western Hemisphere).
• **Spacing:** Maximum at the **Equator (111.32 km)** and converges to zero at the **Poles**.

items.title: 4. Prime Meridian and Time Zones
items.content:
• **Prime Meridian (0°):** Passes through **Greenwich, London** (Royal Observatory); also called the **Greenwich Meridian**.
• **Time Calculation:** Earth rotates 360° in **24 hours** (15° per hour, or 1° in 4 minutes).
• **Eastern Longitudes:** Ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (**GMT**).
• **Western Longitudes:** Behind Greenwich Mean Time (**GMT**).
• **Mnemonic:** **E**ast **A**dvances, **W**est **W**ithdraws (**E**ast is **A**head, **W**est is **W**est/behind).

items.title: 5. Indian Standard Time (IST) and International Date Line
items.content:
• **IST Meridian:** **82.5° E longitude**, passing through **Mirzapur** (near Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh).
• **IST Offset:** **5 hours 30 minutes ahead** of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).
• **International Date Line (IDL):** Located along the **180° meridian**, zig-zagged to avoid splitting island groups.
• **IDL Crossing Rule:** Crossing from East to West adds a day; crossing from West to East subtracts a day.

sections.title: Important Facts and Data
rows: **15° per hour** or **4 minutes per degree**

items.definition: Remember **'LAT is FAT'** — latitudes run horizontally (fat/flat across), while longitudes run vertically up and down like telephone poles.
Remember **'Greenwich = Great'** — Greenwich observatory in London is the starting point (0°) for all longitudes.
Remember **'Eighty-Two and Half'** (82.5° E) — multiply by 4 to get 330 minutes, which equals **5 hours and 30 minutes** ahead of GMT.
Remember **'Torrid, Temperate, Frigid'** (TTF) from Equator to Poles based on sunray angle and latitude bands.
Remember **'Circle = 360°'** — each degree of the Earth's circumference represents one meridian of longitude.
Remember **'IDL is Zig-Zag'** — it bends around Pacific island nations so that countries do not have two different calendar dates on the same landmass.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Latitude Count with Parallel Lines
items.definition: Students often write 180 for latitudes. The correct total is **181** (0° Equator + 90 Northern + 90 Southern).

items.term: Mistake 2: Assuming Longitudes Have Equal Distance Everywhere
items.definition: Longitudes are **widest at the Equator** and converge to a single point at the **North and South Poles**.

items.term: Mistake 3: Getting Confused Between IST and GMT Sign
items.definition: India is in the Eastern Hemisphere, so IST is **ahead (+5:30)** of GMT, never behind.

items.term: Mistake 4: Mixing Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn Degrees
items.definition: Tropic of Cancer is **23.5° N** (Northern Hemisphere, passes through India), while Tropic of Capricorn is **23.5° S** (Southern Hemisphere).

items.term: Mistake 5: Treating International Date Line as a Straight Line
items.definition: IDL is **not a straight 180° line**; it deviates eastward and westward to avoid dividing countries into two different days.

items.term: Mistake 6: Calculating Time in Wrong Direction
items.definition: Moving **East adds time** (gain hours), moving **West subtracts time** (lose hours relative to GMT).
Intersection of **latitudes and longitudes** creates a global grid system used for precise location finding.
The **Equator (0° latitude)** is the longest parallel and divides the globe into northern and southern halves.
Latitudes never intersect each other and remain **equidistant** from one another across the globe.
All longitudes meet at the **North and South Poles**, forming complete great circles when paired.
The **0° longitude** passing through Greenwich acts as the global baseline for calculating time zones.
The world is divided into **24 standard time zones**, each spanning approximately 15° of longitude.
IST is calculated from **82.5° E longitude** passing through Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh.
The **180° meridian** serves as the International Date Line where calendar dates change.
Latitudes determine the **heat zones** (Torrid, Temperate, Frigid) governing global climate patterns.
Questions in UP Assistant Teacher exam frequently test **IST value, time difference, tropic lines, and grid coordinate basics**.

upscNotes.content: Memorize the exact degrees of major latitudes (0°, 23.5° N, 23.5° S, 66.5° N, 66.5° S) as direct factual questions frequently appear in UP teaching exams.
Do not confuse the total number of latitudes (181) with the number of parallel circles excluding poles (179). Standard textbook convention for multiple-choice questions accepts 181.
Practice numerical problems on time zones: given GMT, find IST, or vice versa, using the 4-minutes-per-degree rule.
Students often mix up Mirzapur/Allahabad coordinates with standard Indian states crossed by the Tropic of Cancer (8 states).

keyTakeaways: Latitudes are horizontal parallel circles with a total count of 181.
Longitudes are vertical semi-circles converging at the poles with a total count of 360.
The Prime Meridian (0°) at Greenwich sets global time (GMT).
Indian Standard Time (IST) is 82.5° E, which is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
Earth rotates 15° every hour, equating to 4 minutes per 1° longitude.
The International Date Line (IDL) runs along the 180° meridian and is zig-zagged for administrative convenience.
